questions.question: A supplier's monthly statement is an extract from:
options: The supplier's own DEBTORS ledger — to the supplier, we are a debtor
Our creditors ledger
The supplier's petty cash records
The bank's records

questions.question: What makes the creditors reconciliation different in principle from the bank reconciliation?
options: Only timing differences can arise
The outsider — another ordinary business with an ordinary bookkeeper — may itself be wrong
Our own books are never adjusted
It is performed once a year only

questions.question: The discipline the lesson sets for reading a supplier's statement is:
options: Accept it and pay it immediately
Adjust our books to match it exactly
Read it as a claim to be tested, not an instruction to be obeyed
File it unread until the auditor asks

questions.question: An invoice dated 25 February that only reaches our office on 4 March is an example of:
options: An error by the supplier
An unrecorded discount
Interest wrongly charged
A timing difference that becomes our omission — the goods were received before month end

subtopics.title: Reading the Statement Against the Ledger Account

questions.question: Invoice 3187 for R7 200, for roof sheeting delivered on 25 February but invoiced to us in March, is recorded as:
options: Debit Trading stock, credit Creditors control
Debit Creditors control, credit Trading stock
Debit Interest expense, credit Creditors control
Nothing — it belongs on the reconciliation statement

questions.question: Credit note 244 for R4 100 was entered as R1 400. The correction of R2 700 is:
options: Debit Trading stock, credit Creditors control
Debit Creditors control, credit Trading stock — we reduced the debt by too little
Debit Discount received, credit Creditors control
No entry — the supplier must fix it

questions.question: R2 380 of guttering charged to us but delivered to another customer must be:
options: Journalised as trading stock
Journalised as a sundry loss
Left out of our books entirely and shown on the reconciliation statement, with the supplier queried
Deducted from our next payment without notice

questions.question: Starting at R48 660 and processing the corrections (+R7 200, −R2 700, +R540, −R950), the corrected creditors ledger balance is:
The Creditors Reconciliation Statement runs:
options: From the balance per the statement received to the balance per our corrected creditors ledger account
From the Creditors Control account to the creditors list
From the bank statement to the Bank account
From the pre-adjustment trial balance to the ledger

questions.question: Statement balance R65 930, less payment in transit R10 800, less R2 380 invoiced in error, gives:
Invoice 3187, once recorded in our own books, appears on the reconciliation statement:
options: As an addition to the statement balance
As a deduction from the statement balance
Not at all — the reconciliation statement carries only what remains for the SUPPLIER to do
Twice, once on each side

questions.question: How does this reconciliation differ from last year's control-account reconciliation?
options: It uses percentages instead of rands
It is done only at year end
It covers all creditors at once
Control-against-list is an INTERNAL check; statement-against-ledger-account is EXTERNAL, one supplier at a time

questions.question: Journalising the supplier's R2 380 error in our books would mean:
options: Quietly paying for guttering another business received
Correctly applying prudence
Reducing our creditors balance
Nothing, since the totals still agree

questions.question: Reversing the direction of the understated credit note puts the answer out by:
options: Twice the error — R5 400
Nothing; direction does not matter

questions.question: Interest of R540 charged by the supplier on the overdue account should be:
options: Ignored, because we never asked for it
Deducted from the statement balance
Recorded — debit Interest expense, credit Creditors control — and then queried if it looks wrong
Treated as a discount received

questions.question: Which practice best protects a business against supplier overcharging?
options: Paying every statement in full on the day it arrives
Letting the person who authorises payments also do the reconciliation
Carrying old differences forward until they vanish
Reconciling every statement in the month it arrives and paying from our own corrected ledger account

subtopics.title: The Spaza Owner and the Wholesaler's Bill

questions.question: The lesson's golden rule about a supplier's bill is:
options: It is a claim, not a command
It is always correct
It replaces your own records
It should be paid before it is read

questions.question: The "twist" that separates this from the bank reconciliation is that:
options: There are no timing differences
The wholesaler's clerk is a person, and people put one customer's delivery on another customer's account
Discounts never arise
Interest is never charged

questions.question: The spaza owner's correct response to a bill of R65 930 against an exercise book showing R48 660 is to:
options: Pay the wholesaler's figure
Insist on the exercise book's figure
Sit down with both records and go line by line until every difference is understood
Stop buying from that wholesaler

questions.question: The roof sheeting delivered on the twenty-fifth with the invoice arriving in March means:
options: Your book is short — you have the goods, so add R7 200
Their book is wrong — deduct R7 200 from the statement
Nothing changes anywhere
The sheeting must be sent back

questions.question: The R950 discount allowed for early payment, never written down, means:
options: Your balance is too low; add R950
Your balance is too high; take R950 off
The supplier owes you R950 in cash
It belongs on the reconciliation statement

questions.question: Which two items are "not your problem" and change nothing in your book?
options: The interest and the discount
The invoice and the credit note
The R2 380 invoiced in error and the R10 800 transfer not yet processed
The credit note and the R10 800 transfer

questions.question: The single question to ask about every difference is:
options: Is it big or small?
Which month does it belong to?
Is it a debit or a credit?
Whose book must change?

subtopics.title: Why This Small Job Protects Real Money

questions.question: Paying the R65 930 statement instead of the reconciled R52 750 would mean:
options: Handing a stranger more than thirteen thousand rand you did not owe
Earning a settlement discount
Reducing next month's interest
Nothing — the difference washes out later

questions.question: The question that steers every line of the bridge is:
options: Which journal recorded it?
What does the OTHER side still have to do to this balance?
Is it an asset or a liability?
How old is the item?

questions.question: Why can nobody inside a small business catch a supplier overcharging?
options: Because internal staff are careless
Because the control account hides it
Because nobody inside the business sees the supplier's books — except through this statement
Because overcharging is illegal and therefore rare

questions.question: The lesson's closing warning is that businesses usually:
options: Collapse from one dramatic theft
Lose money mainly through bank charges
Recover any overpayment automatically
Bleed slowly from bills nobody checked
